review_notes: I read the whole file and searched Mathlib's Length.lean and RingTheory for ring-equivalence length transport. Mathlib has LinearEquiv.length_eq and Module.length_eq_of_surjective, but nothing for a semilinear bijection over a ring isomorphism. The target-file lemma is therefore not duplicated by Mathlib. It is duplicated several times inside this repo. I did not check each duplicate's import chain, but this file already uses W23.intrinsic_length_eq_of_ringEquiv and W22.ideal_quotient_length_le_of_bound from the same import cone. I judged the other declarations (the Bezout statement, the torus localization transport and the list/span lemmas) to be specialised, not competing, versions. For Ideal.ofList I found no Mathlib lemma tying it to span of a range. It is unclear whether the W23 copy is called in other files; a grep for a qualified W23 call found nothing.

findings.excerpt:
theorem quotient_length_eq_of_ringEquiv (e : A ≃+* B) (I : Ideal A) (J : Ideal B)
    (hJI : J = I.map e.toRingHom) :
    Module.length A (A ⧸ I) = Module.length B (B ⧸ J) := by
findings.problem: This is the fourth or fifth copy of the same lemma, which says the module length of a quotient is invariant under a ring isomorphism. WeightedTorusJets.W22.quotient_length_eq_of_ringEquiv in ConePrimeLocalization.lean has the same statement up to the name of hJI. Its proof also builds the same semilinear map over e.toRingHom and uses Submodule.orderIsoMapComapOfBijective. W22.length_eq_of_semilinear_bijective already wraps that machinery. Further copies are in Homogenize.lean (WeightedTorusJets.Geometry) and CoordinateLocalizedPrime.lean (DegreeBezout). This file also reaches the same fact by a second route, via W23.intrinsic_length_eq_of_ringEquiv, which calls the W22 lemma. The copy here is not used anywhere in this file and no other file calls it qualified as W23.quotient_length_eq_of_ringEquiv. It is a competing independent declaration with a re-done proof, not a useful named specialisation.
findings.proposed_change: Delete the W23 copy together with its LengthTransport section. Use WeightedTorusJets.W22.quotient_length_eq_of_ringEquiv, which has the identical hypotheses and conclusion, wherever it is needed. More broadly, consolidate the several copies (W22, W23, Geometry, DegreeBezout) into one lemma. Better still, upstream a general semilinear-bijection length lemma next to LinearEquiv.length_eq.
findings.benefit: This removes a duplicated 17-line proof and a possible name clash or ambiguity inside the SiegelZeros namespaces. Readers and downstream users get one canonical lemma for transporting length along a ring isomorphism and do not have to check that several differently-qualified versions agree.
